text: psycopg connection pooling exhaustion: a pool opened per request leaves sockets in CLOSE_WAIT until the kernel reaps them, so size the pool once per process and hand connections back in a finally block.
A long-lived database connection that sat idle through a failover answers the next statement with a terminated-connection error; probe liveness before reusing one.
Autocommit off means every read opens a transaction, and a transaction left open holds the snapshot that blocks vacuum.
Bound parameters are not string formatting: build every WHERE clause with placeholders so the planner can cache the statement and no value can escape its slot.
An idempotent alembic migration pairs every upgrade with a downgrade that actually reverses it, uses IF NOT EXISTS on index creation, and never rewrites a populated table in place.
Adding a NOT NULL column with a default rewrites the whole table on older servers; add it nullable, backfill in batches, then set the constraint.
A schema change that ships ahead of the code that reads it is safe; the reverse order is an outage. Deploy the migration first, always.
Renaming a column is two releases: add the new name and write both, move the readers, then drop the old one.
JWT verification of an expired token must raise TokenExpiredError, never return None: a decoder that answers None on expiry turns an authentication failure into an attribute error three frames away.
Signature checks belong before claim parsing. Reading a claim out of an unverified payload is reading attacker-controlled input.
Clock skew between issuer and verifier makes a short leeway necessary; without one, valid credentials are rejected for seconds after issue.
A session identifier in a log line is a credential in a log line. Redact it at the formatter, not at each call site.
Valkey cache stampede: when a hot key expires, every worker recomputes it at once. Single flight it behind a short lock and let the losers read the value the winner writes.
A write-through cache that stores the computed value before committing the row serves a value no reader can confirm; commit first.
A key namespace without a version prefix cannot be invalidated by deploy; put the schema version in the key.
An unbounded in-process memo is a leak with a hit rate. Give every memo a size cap and evict.

ParadeDB bm25 search: a filter fragment spliced into two statements must not be alias qualified unless both statements alias their table, otherwise the unaliased one cannot be planned and answers an undefined-table error.
A field-qualified match string is required by newer pg_search releases: a bare term is parsed against the key field and errors on anything non-numeric.
Reciprocal rank fusion with a large constant makes adjacent ranks nearly indistinguishable, so a noisy second leg reorders the head of the list.
Scoring one leg and ranking the other mixes units. Fuse ranks with ranks, or scores with scores, never one of each.

Voyage embedding dimension mismatch: a matryoshka truncation to the leading components is not what a typed vector cast does, and a vector(N) cast enforces an exact dimension rather than slicing, so the comparison raises on every call.
Asymmetric models want the query side embedded as a query and the document side as a document; embedding a question as a passage throws away recall for nothing.
Vectors written by two different models share a column but not a space; cosine distance across them is noise. Filter the vector leg to the active model.
A provider that returns nothing when no key is configured is a feature: the caller degrades to lexical search instead of failing the request.
